phenotype_specificity.statement: Patient 1 had a PFAPA-like course and did not meet Behçet's disease criteria; the authors place him and his father in the milder part of the Behçet spectrum. Immunodeficiency work-up was normal; a 400-gene primary-immunodeficiency panel was run, but results for other genes are not stated. 40574834 notes normal IFN scores in carriers of p.E192K or p.C243Y.

quotes.quote: Patient 1 showed a PFAPA-like clinical course with some atypical features but did not fulfill the diagnostic criteria of BD [23].
Therefore, patient 1 and his father with Glu192Lys might be classified as having PFAPA or recurrent stomatitis, which present intermediate or mild severity in BSDs.
He was initially suspected of having an immunodeficiency disease but had no abnormalities in neutrophil function, lymphocyte fraction, or immunoglobulin levels.
Target gene sequencing (TGS) for a primary immunodeficiency-related 400-gene panel was performed using genomic DNA from the whole blood of patients 1 and 2.

Nineteen patients were evaluated for the type I IFN score, of whom 16 patients had an elevated IFN score and three patients carrying missense variants p.E192K or p.C243Y exhibited IFN levels within the normal range (Supplementary Table 2, Supplementary Figure 3).

segregation.statement: One affected relative (father, mild mucocutaneous symptoms) carries the variant. Sanger sequencing was done in the patients and their parents, but the mother's result is not stated explicitly. No unaffected carriers or non-carriers are described.

To confirm the results, Sanger sequencing was performed for the patients and their parents.

functional.statement: Construct studies in A20-deficient HEK293 cells (33549127; wild type, Phe127Cys polymorphism and earlier-reported variants as comparators): Glu192Lys failed to suppress NF-κB reporter activity induced by TNF-α, MYD88 L265P or CARD11 F130V, at any expression level in a Tet-on system; protein expression, IKKβ-mediated Ser381 phosphorylation and TRAF6 deubiquitination were similar to wild type. No patient-cell assay.

quotes.quote: The inhibitory effect on NF-κB reporter gene activity was significantly disrupted by TNFAIP3 Glu192Lys compared with that of WT upon stimulation with TNF-α or co-transfection of MYD88 and CARD11 (Fig. 2a–c).

The variant Glu192Lys could not suppress the increase of activity regardless of the A20 expression level, in contrast to the WT, while the variants Ile310Thr and Gln709Arg suppressed it as well as the WT.
The levels of protein expression for myc-tagged TNFAIP3 variants Glu192Lys and Gln709Arg were similar to the WT expression levels, while that of Ile310Thr was mildly decreased but not abolished.
IKKβ-mediated A20 phosphorylation levels of the variants Glu192Lys, Ile310Thr, and Gln709Arg were similar to that of the WT (Fig. 4b).
The variants Glu192Lys, Ile310Thr, Gln709Arg, and Cys243Tyr did not show differences in deubiquitination from the WT (Fig. 5).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense change, predicted p.(Glu192Lys) (batch HGVS), in the OTU domain. Disease mechanism as stated in the papers: heterozygous loss of function (haploinsufficiency).

quotes.quote: This variant is located in the OTU domain, where many previously reported truncating mutations are located.
AbstractA20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is an autoinflammatory disease caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variations in TNFAIP3, the gene encoding the A20 protein.

As for the p.(Glu192Lys) variant, it does not exhibit reduced expression compared to the WT protein but it loses the ability to sufficiently inhibit the NF-κB pathway (Kadowaki et al., 2021), in line with its location at the putative ubiquitin-binding site of A20 (Lin et al., 2008).

computational_predictions.statement: As reported: PolyPhen-2 0.999 ('probably damaging'), CADD 32, SIFT not available; Glu192 in a highly conserved region (BLAST alignment). 37342083 adds PremPS ΔΔG 0.65 kcal/mol and structure modelling of altered contacts (Lys192 with Leu171 and Met174).

quotes.quote: Regarding Glu192Lys, in silico analysis identified this variant as probably damaging with a score of 0.999 in Polyphen-2 and 32 in CADD (Table 2 and Supplementary Fig. S1).

As for the missense variations located in the OTU domain, the pathogenic significance is demonstrated for four of them: p.(Glu192Lys) (Kadowaki et al., 2021), p.(Leu236Pro) (reported in this study), p.(Cys243Tyr) (Shigemura et al., 2016), and p.(Leu275Pro) (Aslani et al., 2022) and, which all fulfill the ACMG criteria for pathogenicity (Richards et al., 2015).
All 54 patients analyzed had heterozygous variants in TNFAIP3, comprising a total of 35 distinct pathogenic variants.

concerns: Likely duplicate identities: 33549127 Patient 1 (HA20-ID0097), 37342083 Table 2 column 4 index case (HA20-ID0618) and 40574834 P20 (HA20-ID0721) are probably one boy; 33549127 father / 37342083 father (HA20-ID0100) and 40574834 P21 (HA20-ID0342) are probably one man. Evidence: 37342083 column 4 cites Kadowaki et al. 2021 (= 33549127) with the same onset (11 months) and father description; 40574834 cites reference 2 (= Kadowaki 2021) for family F10, and P20 has the same onset (11 mo), PFAPA diagnosis, cimetidine and tonsillectomy.

Contradiction on mucosal ulcers: 37342083 lists 'Aphthous stomatitis' for the index case, while 33549127 Table 1 lists 'Recurrent fever, pharyngitis, coxitis' and 40574834 lists no oral/genital ulcer (−/−) for P20. The father has 'recurrent stomatitis' in 33549127 but P21 is listed with ulcers −/− in 40574834.
Mother's genotype is not stated, although both parents were Sanger-sequenced.
The functional profile is mixed: loss of NF-κB inhibition, but normal expression, Ser381 phosphorylation and deubiquitinase activity.
33549127 aligns protein against NP_001257437.1; 37342083 uses NM_006290 (no version).
notes_for_panel: One family (affected boy and mildly affected father) reported three times, plus construct functional data and in-silico/population statements from 33549127, re-tabulated in the 37342083 review.
